Title: Welcome to Yorkshire chairman Peter Box  U-turns on resignation - Hull Live
# Welcome to Yorkshire chairman Peter Box U-turns on resignation. Embattled Welcome to Yorkshire chairman Peter Box will remain in post. Embattled Welcome to Yorkshire chairman Peter Box will remain in post(Image: Daniel Oxtoby/Hull Live). Welcome to Yorkshire chairman Peter Box has backtracked on plans to resign after an emergency meeting at the organisation which lost half its board through protest resignations in September. Mr Box, a former leader of Wakefield Council, had previously announced he would step down as chairman at a meeting at the start of November. **For the latest politics news in Hull and East Yorkshire, click here.**. That AGM has now been postponed indefinitely until local councils and others who provide the funding that keeps Welcome to Yorkshire afloat have their say on the future of the organisation. This means that the embattled Mr Box will remain in his position overseeing the management of the agency through these turbulent times. James Mason, chief executive, Welcome to Yorkshire. James Mason's departure as chief executive of Welcome to Yorkshire triggered a wave of resignations (Image: Welcome to Yorkshire). At the meeting held on Thursday, October 21, Mr Box said: “The board have in private reviewed both the organisation’s finances and its commercial plan" reports The Yorkshire Post. He continued: “The board are confident that the team are working hard to ensure the future of Welcome to Yorkshire. The board are unanimous in saying there is a need for a Yorkshire-wide DMO [Destination Marketing Organisation]. In the circumstances, the board have agreed the AGM be postponed until that consultation has been completed. “The board can confirm that interim arrangements regarding the organisation’s leadership will be dealt with expeditiously and any interim appointment would include board membership.”. The announcement last month, that chief executive James Mason would be leaving the organisation, was followed by half of the eight-person board resigning in protest. Mr Mason was appointed as chief executive in December 2019 following the departure of Sir Gary Verity, his appointment came after the agency faced widespread criticism of how it was financed and managed. During an expenses scandal following the resignation of chief executive Sir Gary Verity, Welcome to Yorkshire had the shell out nearly £500,000.

Jason Wells, CEO and COO of CenterPoint Energy, testified before the Senate Select Committee on Hurricane and Tropical Storm Preparedness, Recovery, and Electricity, July 29, 2024. A Senate select committee questioned Jason Wells, the CEO and chief operating officer of CenterPoint Energy, for hours on Monday regarding the utility's response to Hurricane Beryl. Houston Senator Paul Bettencourt, among others, grilled Wells on issues ranging from CenterPoint's failure to restore its outage tracker before Beryl; to the five-year timeframe for CenterPoint to trim back vegetation, which is roughly 4 ½ years from completion; to the usefulness of its $800-million purchase of mobile generators, which to date have gone unused.
